Estate tax applies to a deceased person's property, excise tax applies to specific goods such as gasoline, and property tax is based on the value of real estate owned.
w: Estate tax applies to a deceased person's property before it passes to heirs, but Priya earned her profit by selling stock while she was alive.
Excise tax is charged on specific goods such as gasoline or tobacco, not on the profit from selling shares of stock.
Property tax is based on the value of real estate someone owns, while Priya's $1,800 came from selling stock for more than she paid.

q.pt: Discuss the effect of tax laws and regulations on financial transactions
q.s: When Harold Brennan died, the total value of his assets was calculated, and a tax was paid out of those assets before the remaining property was distributed to his children. This tax is
q.r: An estate tax. An estate tax is a tax on the value of a deceased person's property, paid from the estate before the remaining assets pass to heirs. Estate tax laws affect how people plan to transfer wealth. A gift tax applies to transfers made while the giver is living, a capital gains tax applies to profits from selling assets, and a luxury tax applies to expensive, nonessential goods.
w: A gift tax applies to transfers made while the giver is still living, but this tax was paid from Harold's assets after his death.
A capital gains tax applies to profit from selling an asset, while this tax was based on the total value of Harold's assets at his death.
A luxury tax is added to the sale of expensive, nonessential goods, not to the value of property left behind when someone dies.

q.pt: Discuss the effect of tax laws and regulations on financial transactions
q.s: A government adds an extra tax to the sale of yachts, private jets and very expensive automobiles, but not to everyday necessities. This is an example of
q.r: A luxury tax. A luxury tax is placed on expensive, nonessential goods that mainly wealthier buyers purchase, such as yachts and high-end cars, while necessities are left untaxed. Because it raises the price of these items, it can affect buyers' purchase and financing decisions. A property tax is based on the value of real estate, a payroll tax is withheld from wages, and an estate tax applies to a deceased person's property.
w: A property tax is based on the value of real estate a person owns, not added to the sale of yachts, jets and expensive cars.
A payroll tax is withheld from workers' wages, so it is not an extra charge placed on purchases of high-priced, nonessential goods.
An estate tax applies to a deceased person's property, while this tax is charged when people buy yachts, jets and costly automobiles.

q.pt: Discuss the effect of tax laws and regulations on financial transactions
q.s: This year, Jordan earned a $4,500 gain selling shares of Fenwick Corp. and had a $1,200 loss selling shares of Ardent Co. He held both investments for more than one year. After offsetting the gain with the loss, what is his net capital gain?
q.r: $3,300. Tax law allows capital losses to offset capital gains, so only the net gain is taxed: $4,500 gain - $1,200 loss = $3,300. Offsetting lowers the amount of profit subject to capital gains tax. $5,700 wrongly adds the loss to the gain, $4,500 ignores the loss entirely, and $1,200 is only the amount of the loss.
w: $5,700 comes from adding the $1,200 loss to the $4,500 gain, but a loss reduces the taxable gain, so it must be subtracted instead.
$4,500 is just the gain from Fenwick Corp. with the $1,200 loss ignored, but tax law lets Jordan use that loss to lower his gain.
$1,200 is only the amount of the Ardent Co. loss; the net gain comes from subtracting that loss from the $4,500 gain.

q.pt: Discuss the effect of tax laws and regulations on financial transactions
q.s: Darius, who is in a high income tax bracket, buys bonds issued by cities in his state instead of corporate bonds that pay slightly higher interest. Which tax rule most likely explains his choice?
o: Gains from selling municipal bonds are exempt from capital gains tax.
Municipal bond interest is generally exempt from federal income tax.
Corporate bond interest is taxed only in the year the bond is sold.
Corporate bonds can be purchased only through retirement accounts.
q.r: Municipal bond interest is generally exempt from federal income tax. Interest on bonds issued by state and local governments is usually free of federal income tax and often of state income tax for in-state buyers. For an investor in a high tax bracket, this tax break can make a lower-rate municipal bond more profitable after taxes than a corporate bond. Profits from selling municipal bonds are subject to capital gains tax, corporate bond interest is taxed each year as it is received, and corporate bonds can be bought in any type of account.
w: Profits from selling municipal bonds are generally subject to capital gains tax; the main tax break Darius gets is on the interest the bonds pay each year.
Corporate bond interest is usually taxed each year as it is received, not only when the bond is sold, so this would not explain Darius's choice.
Corporate bonds can be bought in ordinary taxable accounts as well as retirement accounts, so this is not a real rule that would steer Darius's decision.

q.pt: Discuss the effect of tax laws and regulations on financial transactions
q.s: Kenji puts money he has already paid income tax on into a retirement account. If he follows the account's rules, his withdrawals in retirement will be tax-free. Kenji is most likely using a
q.r: Roth IRA. A Roth IRA is funded with after-tax dollars, and qualified withdrawals in retirement, including earnings, are tax-free. Tax rules like these shape how people save and invest. Contributions to a traditional 401(k) or traditional IRA are generally made before taxes, and withdrawals are taxed later. A taxable brokerage account offers no special tax break, so its gains and dividends are taxed.
w: A traditional 401(k) is usually funded with money before taxes, and withdrawals are taxed later, which is the opposite of what Kenji is doing.
A traditional IRA generally gives a tax break when money goes in and taxes withdrawals in retirement, while Kenji's withdrawals will be tax-free.
A taxable brokerage account has no special retirement tax break, so Kenji would owe tax on gains and dividends instead of withdrawing tax-free.

q.pt: Discuss the effect of tax laws and regulations on financial transactions
q.s: While she is living, Gloria transfers ownership of her $400,000 vacation home to her nephew without asking for any payment. Which federal tax law covers this kind of transfer?
q.r: Gift tax. Federal gift tax law covers transfers of money or property from a living person to someone else without full payment in return, and the giver is responsible for reporting large gifts. Gift tax rules discourage people from avoiding estate tax by giving everything away before death. Estate tax applies to property transferred at death, sales tax applies to retail purchases, and excise tax applies to specific goods such as gasoline.
w: Estate tax applies to property transferred when someone dies, but Gloria is giving away her vacation home while she is still living.
Sales tax is charged on retail purchases, and Gloria's nephew is not buying anything because she asked for no payment.
Excise tax applies to specific goods such as gasoline or tobacco, not to a living person giving away a house for free.

q.pt: Describe the use of technology in compliance
q.s: What is the main benefit of using technology to manage a bank's compliance activities?
o: Greater efficiency in completing compliance tasks
Fewer regulations that apply to the bank
Less need to train employees on policies
Higher interest rates on customer loans
q.r: Greater efficiency in completing compliance tasks. Compliance technology automates routine work such as monitoring transactions, gathering data and preparing regulatory reports, so tasks are completed faster and with fewer resources. Technology does not change which regulations apply to a bank, employees still need training on policies, and loan interest rates are set by the bank's lending decisions and market conditions, not by compliance software.
w: Technology helps a bank follow its regulations faster, but it does not change which laws and rules apply to the bank in the first place.
Compliance software can automate tasks, but employees still need training so they understand the bank's policies and follow them in their daily work.
Loan interest rates depend on the bank's lending decisions and market conditions, not on the software it uses to manage compliance work.

q.pt: Describe the use of technology in compliance
q.s: Tri-County Savings uses artificial intelligence software to review millions of transactions and flag unusual activity that may signal money laundering. This technology mainly helps the bank by
o: setting the interest rates on customer accounts.
spotting patterns and trends in large amounts of data.
deciding which laws the bank must follow.
marketing new services to existing customers.
q.r: Spotting patterns and trends in large amounts of data. Artificial intelligence can analyze far more transactions than people can and flag patterns, such as unusual transfers, that may point to money laundering or fraud. Compliance staff then investigate the flagged activity. The software does not set interest rates, laws and regulators determine which rules apply, and marketing new services is a sales function rather than a compliance one.
w: Interest rates on accounts are set by the bank's pricing decisions and market conditions, not by software that reviews transactions for signs of money laundering.
Laws and regulators decide which rules Tri-County Savings must follow; the software only helps the bank check its transactions against those rules.
Marketing new services is a sales job, while this software is reviewing transactions to flag activity that might signal money laundering.

q.pt: Describe the use of technology in compliance
q.s: Lomax Insurance switched from typing regulatory reports by hand to software that pulls data directly from its systems. Which compliance benefit is the company most likely to see?
o: An exemption from state insurance exams
Fewer human errors in its reports
q.r: Fewer human errors in its reports. When software pulls data straight from a firm's systems, it removes manual typing and calculation steps where mistakes often occur, so regulatory reports are more accurate. Compliance technology does not raise premiums, insurers remain subject to state regulators' examinations, and automating reports reduces handwritten records rather than adding to them.
w: Report software does not raise the premiums policyholders pay, which are based on risk and pricing decisions, not on how regulatory reports are prepared.
Lomax still has to go through state insurance exams; better report software improves accuracy but does not excuse the company from regulators' reviews.
Switching to software that pulls data automatically means fewer handwritten records, not more, since the reports are no longer typed or written by hand.

q.pt: Describe the use of technology in compliance
q.s: Software and other technology that help financial firms monitor activity, file reports and meet regulatory requirements are known as
q.r: Regulatory technology (regtech). Regtech is technology designed to help firms meet regulatory requirements, using tools such as automated monitoring, data analytics and reporting software to make compliance faster and less costly. Customer relationship management systems organize customer information, electronic funds transfer moves money between accounts electronically, and enterprise resource planning software links a company's business processes.
w: Customer relationship management tools organize customer contacts and sales information, not the monitoring and reporting needed to meet regulatory requirements.
Electronic funds transfer moves money between accounts electronically, but it is not a set of tools for monitoring activity and filing regulatory reports.
Enterprise resource planning software links a company's business processes like purchasing and accounting, but it is not built specifically to help meet regulatory requirements.

q.pt: Describe the use of technology in compliance
q.s: Hartwell Credit Union automated its routine regulatory checks, so compliance staff now finish in hours work that once took weeks. Besides saving time, this change is most likely to
o: shift legal responsibility for compliance to regulators.
increase the number of rules the credit union must follow.
reduce the credit union's need for deposit insurance.
lower the credit union's compliance costs.
q.r: Lower the credit union's compliance costs. Automating routine checks reduces the staff hours and manual effort that compliance requires, so the credit union spends less to meet the same rules. Lower cost is a major benefit of compliance technology. The credit union remains legally responsible for compliance, technology does not add regulations, and deposit insurance is unrelated to how compliance work is performed.
w: Automating checks speeds up the work, but Hartwell Credit Union stays legally responsible for following the rules; regulators do not take over that responsibility.
Automation changes how the credit union does its compliance work, not how many rules apply; regulators, not software, decide the number of rules.
Deposit insurance protects members' savings if a credit union fails, and how quickly compliance checks are done does not change that need.

q.pt: Discuss the nature and scope of compliance in the finance industry
q.s: Each month, a Pinecrest Bank employee who does not handle cash compares the bank's records with its bank statements to find any errors or irregularities that have already occurred. This reconciliation is an example of a(n) __________ control.
q.r: Detective. A detective control is an internal control that finds errors, fraud or other problems after they have occurred, and account reconciliations and audits are common examples. Finding problems allows the bank to fix them and improve its processes. Preventive controls stop problems before they happen, corrective controls fix problems once they are found, and directive controls, such as written policies, tell employees what to do.
w: Preventive controls stop problems before they happen, but this monthly reconciliation looks for errors and irregularities that Pinecrest Bank has already experienced.
Corrective controls fix problems once they are found, while this reconciliation is the step that finds the problems in the first place.
Directive controls, like written policies, tell employees what to do, but comparing records to bank statements is a check for mistakes already made.

q.pt: Discuss the nature and scope of compliance in the finance industry
q.s: Rivermark Bank requires two employees to approve any wire transfer over $50,000 before it is sent, which helps stop fraud and errors before they happen. This requirement is a __________ control.
q.r: Preventive. A preventive control is designed to stop errors or fraud before they occur. Requiring a second approval means no single employee can send a large transfer alone. Detective controls, such as audits, find problems after they happen, corrective controls fix problems once they are discovered, and compensating controls are backup measures used when a primary control cannot be put in place.
w: Detective controls find problems after they occur, such as audits, but Rivermark's second approval happens before a transfer is ever sent.
Corrective controls fix problems once they are discovered, while the two-person approval is meant to stop fraud and errors before any transfer goes out.
Compensating controls are backup measures used when a main control cannot be put in place, but the two-person approval here is itself the main control.

q.pt: Discuss the nature and scope of compliance in the finance industry
q.s: Which of the following is an example of an activity included in a financial firm's compliance function:
o: Setting the prices of the firm's investment products
Choosing an agency for the firm's advertising
Designing internal controls to meet regulatory requirements
q.r: Designing internal controls to meet regulatory requirements. A financial firm's compliance function identifies the laws and regulations that apply, assesses risk, designs internal controls and policies, trains employees, monitors activity and reports to regulators. Setting product prices is a pricing decision, choosing an advertising agency is a marketing decision, and forecasting interest rates is economic analysis rather than compliance work.
w: Setting prices for investment products is a pricing and business decision, not part of making sure the firm follows laws and regulations.
Choosing an advertising agency is a marketing decision; the compliance function focuses on meeting legal and regulatory requirements rather than picking vendors for ads.
Forecasting interest rates is economic analysis that helps with planning, but it is not about designing controls to make sure the firm obeys regulations.

q.pt: Discuss the nature and scope of compliance in the finance industry
q.s: Westbrook Securities repeatedly failed to file required reports with regulators on time. Which of the following is a likely consequence of this noncompliance?
o: Lower insurance premiums for the firm
Fewer regulatory audits in the future
Greater confidence among the firm's investors
Fines and damage to the firm's reputation
q.r: Fines and damage to the firm's reputation. Noncompliance with financial regulations can lead to penalties, closer regulatory scrutiny and additional audits, lawsuits, and reputational damage that drives customers away. A firm with a record of violations would expect more audits, not fewer, and investors would lose confidence rather than gain it. Rule violations also tend to raise a firm's risk profile rather than lower its insurance premiums.
w: Repeated rule violations make Westbrook look riskier, so its insurance premiums would be more likely to rise than fall.
A firm that keeps missing filing deadlines draws closer attention from regulators, so Westbrook should expect more audits, not fewer.
Missing required reports makes investors worry about how well the firm is run, so their confidence would drop rather than grow.

q.pt: Discuss the nature and scope of compliance in the finance industry
q.s: Why is a strong compliance program important to banks and other financial institutions?
o: It helps maintain public trust in the institution.
It raises the returns on customers' investments.
It reduces the income taxes the institution owes.
It replaces the need for deposit insurance.
q.r: It helps maintain public trust in the institution. Customers hand banks their savings and personal data, so they need confidence that the institution follows the law and protects them. A strong compliance program supports that trust and helps the institution avoid penalties. Compliance does not raise investment returns, does not lower income taxes, and does not take the place of deposit insurance.
w: Investment returns depend on markets and the choices investors make, and following the rules does not make customers' investments earn more.
Income taxes are set by tax law, and a compliance program does not lower what the institution owes; it helps the institution avoid penalties instead.
Deposit insurance protects customers' savings if a bank fails, and a compliance program cannot take its place even if it lowers the chance of problems.

q.pt: Explain the responsibilities of finance professionals in providing client services
q.s: A client calls Dana, a bank relationship manager, upset that a transfer she requested was processed a week late because of a bank error. To keep the client's loyalty, what is Dana's best response?
o: Explain that delays are common in banking
Ask the client to file a written complaint
Refer the client to the bank's legal department
Apologize and correct the problem right away
q.r: Apologize and correct the problem right away. When the firm is at fault, a sincere apology followed by prompt action shows the client that the relationship matters and is the best way to keep the client's loyalty. Excusing the delay as common, adding paperwork for the client, or passing the client to the legal department makes the client feel unimportant and risks losing the relationship.
w: Calling delays common makes excuses for the bank's own mistake, which tells the client the error does not matter and can push the client to leave.
Asking the client to file a written complaint adds work for someone already upset about the bank's error, instead of Dana taking responsibility and fixing the problem directly.
Sending the client to the legal department makes a simple service error feel like a dispute and shows the bank is not taking responsibility.

q.pt: Explain the responsibilities of finance professionals in providing client services
q.s: What is a financial planner's primary responsibility to clients?
o: Selling the products that pay the planner the highest commissions
Promoting the firm's newest investment products to every client
Providing financial guidance that fits each client's needs and goals
Managing each client's household budget every month
q.r: Providing financial guidance that fits each client's needs and goals. A financial planner's core responsibility is to understand each client's situation, goals and risk tolerance and to give appropriate advice in the client's interest. Recommending products based on commissions or the firm's latest offerings puts the planner or firm first, and planners advise on budgeting rather than managing clients' monthly household spending for them.
w: Choosing products by the commission they pay puts the planner's own income ahead of the client's needs, which goes against the planner's main duty.
Pushing the firm's newest products to every client ignores that each client has different goals, so it serves the firm rather than the client.
Planners may advise clients on budgeting, but they do not run each client's household spending every month; their main job is fitting guidance to each client's goals.

q.pt: Explain the responsibilities of finance professionals in providing client services
q.s: Before recommending any services, an insurance agent wants to be sure she can meet a new client's needs. Which topic is most important for her to ask the client about?
o: The level of service the client expects
The fees the client's previous agent charged
Other clients of hers the client may know
Friends the client could refer to her
q.r: The level of service the client expects. Learning a client's service expectations, such as how often to meet, how to communicate and how involved the client wants to be, lets the professional deliver the service the client values. Asking about a previous agent's fees, about other clients, or about possible referrals before providing any service does not reveal how to serve this client well.
w: The previous agent's fees might matter for pricing, but they tell the agent little about how this new client wants to be served going forward.
Asking which of her other clients the new client knows does not help the agent understand what this client needs from her.
Asking for referrals before providing any service puts the agent's business growth ahead of learning what the new client actually needs.

q.pt: Explain the responsibilities of finance professionals in providing client services
q.s: Jordan, a financial planner, works hard to keep his clients satisfied. Besides repeat business, satisfied clients are most likely to benefit Jordan by
q.r: Referring new clients to him. Satisfied clients tend to recommend their advisor to friends, family and coworkers, and these referrals are one of the most effective and least costly ways for a finance professional to grow a client base. Client satisfaction does not change licensing or continuing education requirements, and a client's risk tolerance depends on the client's goals and situation, not on satisfaction.
w: Licensing requirements are set by regulators, so having happy clients does not lower the requirements Jordan must meet to work as a planner.
Continuing education hours are required by regulators and professional organizations, and client satisfaction does not reduce how many hours Jordan must complete.
How much risk a client should take depends on the client's goals and situation, not on how satisfied the client is with Jordan's service.

q.pt: Explain the responsibilities of finance professionals in providing client services
q.s: When explaining a variable annuity to a client with little investing experience, a financial advisor should
o: use technical terms to show her expertise.
hand over the prospectus without discussion.
use simple, clear language and avoid jargon.
q.r: Use simple, clear language and avoid jargon. Clients must understand a product's features, costs and risks to make informed decisions, so finance professionals explain products in plain language suited to the client's knowledge. Technical jargon confuses clients, handing over a prospectus without explanation leaves questions unanswered, and stressing best-case returns gives an unbalanced picture of the product's risks.
w: Technical terms may sound impressive, but they would confuse a client with little investing experience who needs to understand the annuity's costs and risks.
A prospectus contains important details, but handing it over without discussion leaves an inexperienced client to sort through complex material alone.
Stressing only best-case returns gives the client an unbalanced picture, hiding the risks a variable annuity can carry when investments lose value.

q.pt: Explain the responsibilities of finance professionals in providing client services
q.s: Mason, a financial planner, has not kept up with recent changes in retirement-account rules and gives a client outdated advice. Which professional standard has Mason failed to meet?
q.r: Competence. Competence means maintaining the knowledge and skills needed to serve clients, which requires keeping up with changing laws, rules and products. Mason's outdated advice shows he has not stayed current. Confidentiality concerns protecting client information, objectivity means giving impartial advice free of conflicts of interest, and fairness means treating clients equitably and disclosing material conflicts.
w: Confidentiality means protecting client information, but Mason's problem is that his knowledge of retirement-account rules is out of date.
Objectivity means giving advice free of conflicts of interest, while Mason's outdated advice comes from not keeping his knowledge current, not from bias.
Fairness means treating clients equally and disclosing conflicts, but Mason's failure is a lack of up-to-date knowledge rather than unequal treatment.

q.pt: Explain the responsibilities of finance professionals in providing client services
q.s: Without the client's permission, an accountant at Delgado & Price describes a client's income and debts to a friend over dinner. Which professional responsibility has the accountant violated?
q.r: Confidentiality. Finance professionals have a duty to protect clients' personal and financial information and to share it only with the client's permission or when the law requires. Discussing a client's income and debts socially breaks that trust. Competence concerns up-to-date knowledge, diligence means prompt and thorough work, and objectivity means impartial advice free of conflicts of interest.
w: Competence means keeping knowledge and skills up to date, but the accountant's problem is sharing a client's private financial details, not a lack of skill.
Diligence means doing work promptly and thoroughly, while the accountant's mistake was revealing a client's income and debts to a friend.
Objectivity means giving advice free of conflicts of interest, but discussing a client's finances over dinner is about protecting private information.

q.pt: Explain the responsibilities of finance professionals in providing client services
q.s: Financial advisor Lena recommends that a client invest in a company owned by her brother, without telling the client about the relationship. Lena's recommendation most likely violates the standard of
q.r: Objectivity. Objectivity requires finance professionals to give impartial advice and to disclose conflicts of interest that could influence their recommendations. Lena's family tie to the company is an undisclosed conflict of interest that may bias her advice. Competence concerns current knowledge and skills, confidentiality concerns protecting client information, and diligence concerns prompt, thorough work.
w: Competence concerns having current knowledge and skills, but Lena's problem is a hidden family connection that could bias her advice.
Confidentiality is about protecting client information, while Lena's issue is failing to disclose her brother's ownership of the company she recommends.
Diligence means doing work promptly and thoroughly, but the problem with Lena's recommendation is an undisclosed conflict of interest.

q.pt: Use Customer Relationship Management (CRM) technology
q.s: What is the main benefit a bank gains from using a customer relationship management (CRM) system?
q.r: Improved customer service. A CRM system gathers each customer's contact details, accounts and interaction history in one place, so employees can respond quickly, personalize service and anticipate needs. Better service builds loyalty and retention. Loan interest rates depend on market conditions and the bank's lending policies, payroll is a human resources function, and building maintenance is unrelated to CRM.
w: Loan interest rates depend on market conditions and the bank's lending policies, not on software that organizes customer information and interactions.
Payroll is a human resources task handled by payroll software; a CRM system focuses on customers, not on paying employees.
Building maintenance costs have nothing to do with a system that stores customer contacts, accounts and interaction history.

q.pt: Use Customer Relationship Management (CRM) technology
q.s: Which of the following is an example of information a brokerage firm typically stores in its CRM system:
o: Sales opportunities with current and prospective clients
The terms of the firm's office lease agreements
q.r: Sales opportunities with current and prospective clients. CRM systems store customer-facing information such as contact details, interaction history, account information, preferences and sales opportunities, so the firm can track potential business through to a sale. Office leases, payroll tax withholdings and equipment maintenance records are internal business records kept in other systems, not customer relationship data.
w: Office lease terms are internal business records about the firm's property, not information about the firm's relationships with clients.
Employees' payroll tax withholdings are kept in payroll systems, since a CRM system stores information about customers rather than staff.
Maintenance records for office equipment are internal operating records, not customer data that would help the brokerage manage client relationships.

q.pt: Use Customer Relationship Management (CRM) technology
q.s: How can a CRM strategy help a credit union increase its revenue?
o: By reducing the number of products it offers
By helping it offer members the products they want
By replacing member service staff with forms
By limiting how often it contacts members
q.r: By helping it offer members the products they want. CRM data shows each member's accounts, needs and past interactions, so the credit union can offer the right product at the right time, which increases sales and keeps members loyal. Cutting products, replacing service staff with forms, or reducing contact with members would weaken relationships and give members fewer reasons to do more business with the credit union.
w: Offering fewer products gives members fewer reasons to do more business with the credit union, which would shrink revenue rather than grow it.
Replacing service staff with forms weakens personal relationships, while a CRM strategy uses member information to serve people better and offer what they need.
Contacting members less often means fewer chances to offer useful products, which works against the CRM goal of building stronger relationships.

q.pt: Use Customer Relationship Management (CRM) technology
q.s: A wealth management firm discovers that many client records in its CRM system have outdated addresses and duplicate entries. Correcting and removing these records is called
q.r: Data cleansing. Data cleansing is the process of finding and correcting or removing inaccurate, outdated, incomplete or duplicate records so a database stays accurate and useful. Clean CRM data lets employees contact the right client at the right address. Data mining searches large data sets for patterns, data encryption scrambles data to protect it, and data backup copies data so it can be restored if lost.
w: Data mining searches large data sets for hidden patterns, but the firm is fixing outdated addresses and removing duplicates, which is cleaning the data.
Data encryption scrambles data to protect it from unauthorized readers, but it does not correct outdated addresses or remove duplicate records.
Data backup copies records so they can be restored if lost, but backing up bad records would only save the same errors and duplicates.

q.pt: Use Customer Relationship Management (CRM) technology
q.s: Brightline Financial sets its CRM system to remind each advisor automatically when a client's annual portfolio review is due. This use of CRM technology mainly helps the firm
o: follow up with clients consistently and on time.
eliminate the need for face-to-face client meetings.
set the fees that clients pay for portfolio reviews.
reduce the number of clients each advisor serves.
q.r: Follow up with clients consistently and on time. CRM systems can automate tasks such as scheduling reminders, so advisors contact each client when a review or follow-up is due instead of relying on memory. Consistent, timely contact shows clients they are valued and strengthens the relationship. Reminders support rather than replace personal meetings, fees are set by the firm's pricing policies, and automation helps advisors serve their clients efficiently rather than limiting how many they serve.
w: Automatic reminders help advisors schedule reviews, but they support personal meetings rather than replace them, so Brightline still meets with clients face to face.
Review fees are set by Brightline's pricing policies, while the reminder only tells advisors when a client's annual review is due.
Reminders help each advisor keep up with clients more efficiently, which supports serving more clients rather than reducing how many each advisor serves.

q.pt: Use Customer Relationship Management (CRM) technology
q.s: In his bank's CRM system, loan officer Theo sees that a longtime client recently opened a business checking account and asked a teller about equipment financing. What is Theo's best next step?
o: Delete the inquiry from the client's record
Send the client a general bank newsletter
Wait until the client applies at a branch
Contact the client about a business equipment loan
q.r: Contact the client about a business equipment loan. CRM technology is valuable because it turns recorded interactions into action: the system shows a sales opportunity, and a timely, relevant offer serves the client and builds revenue. Deleting the inquiry loses useful data, a general newsletter ignores the client's specific need, and waiting risks losing the client to another lender.
w: Deleting the inquiry throws away useful information about the client's needs, which defeats the purpose of recording interactions in the CRM system.
A general newsletter ignores the specific interest the client showed in equipment financing, so it misses the clear sales opportunity Theo spotted.
Waiting for the client to apply risks losing the business to another lender, even though the CRM system already shows what the client needs.

q.pt: Use Customer Relationship Management (CRM) technology
q.s: When client Ruth Chen calls Northgate Insurance, the agent immediately sees Ruth's past claims, recent emails and policy renewal date on one screen. This is made possible by
q.r: Customer relationship management (CRM) software. CRM software brings each customer's contact information, interaction history and account details together in one place, so any employee can serve the customer quickly and personally. General ledger software records the firm's accounting transactions, payroll software calculates employee pay, and inventory management software tracks stock levels.
w: General ledger software records the firm's accounting transactions, but it does not show an agent a client's past claims, emails and renewal date on one screen.
Payroll software calculates employee pay, so it would not hold Ruth Chen's claims history, recent emails or policy renewal date.
Inventory management software tracks stock levels of goods, not a client's claims, communications and policy details.

q.pt: Demonstrate advanced database applications
q.s: A credit union's database stores each member's mailing address in three different tables, which causes errors when a member moves. The database team reorganizes the tables so the address is stored only once. This process is called
q.r: Normalization. Normalization organizes a relational database's tables so each fact is stored in only one place, which removes redundant data and prevents the inconsistencies that occur when copies are updated separately. Data filtering displays only records that meet criteria, data mining searches data for patterns, and sorting arranges records in a particular order.
w: Data filtering only displays records that meet certain criteria, but it does not change how tables are set up to store each address once.
Data mining searches data for hidden patterns, while the team is restructuring tables to remove repeated addresses that cause errors.
Sorting puts records in a certain order, but the addresses would still be stored in three tables, so the errors after a move would remain.

q.pt: Demonstrate advanced database applications
q.s: To prevent entry errors, a bank's loan database rejects any value in the Interest Rate field that is below 0% or above 30%. This database feature is a(n)
q.r: Validation rule. A validation rule is a condition that data must meet before a database accepts it, such as a value falling within a set range. Validation rules protect data integrity by stopping obvious entry errors at the source. An index speeds up searching and sorting, a join links related tables through a shared field, and a query retrieves records that meet criteria rather than checking new entries.
w: An index speeds up searching and sorting records, but it does not check whether a new interest rate falls between 0% and 30%.
A join links related tables through a shared field, while this feature checks each new entry against a set range before accepting it.
A query pulls out records that meet certain conditions after data is stored, but it does not reject bad entries as they are typed in.

q.pt: Demonstrate advanced database applications
q.s: An analyst at Granite Bank needs a report that combines data from the Customers, Loans and Branches tables. What should she do first?
o: Join all three tables on every field
Define exactly what information the report needs
Sort the Loans table by balance
Export the tables to a spreadsheet
q.r: Define exactly what information the report needs. Building a multi-table query starts with a clear statement of the business question, which determines the tables, fields, joins and criteria to use. Joining every field produces meaningless results, and sorting or exporting tables before knowing what is needed wastes time and may leave out required data.
w: Joining all three tables on every field would produce meaningless results; the analyst should first know what the report needs, then join only on related fields.
Sorting the Loans table before knowing what the report must show is wasted effort, since the report's needs decide which data and order matter.
Exporting the tables to a spreadsheet before deciding what is needed may waste time and leave out data the report actually requires.

q.pt: Demonstrate advanced database applications
q.s: A financial analyst displays only the transactions over $10,000 from the past quarter, temporarily hiding all other records. The analyst is using
q.r: Data filtering. Data filtering selects a subset of records that meet specified criteria, such as amount and date, so the user can analyze only the data that matters for the question. Normalization restructures tables to remove redundancy, data cleansing corrects or removes bad records, and data encryption protects data by scrambling it.
w: Normalization reorganizes tables to remove repeated data, but the analyst is only temporarily showing large recent transactions and hiding the rest.
Data cleansing fixes or removes inaccurate records permanently, while the analyst is just hiding records that do not meet the amount and date criteria.
Data encryption scrambles data to protect it, but it does not choose which transactions appear on the analyst's screen.

q.pt: Demonstrate advanced database applications
q.s: A brokerage wants a list of its clients in Ohio who made more than 20 trades last year so it can offer them a lower-commission plan. Which query criteria should the analyst use?
o: State = Ohio and trades last year > 20
State = Ohio or trades last year > 20
q.r: State = Ohio and trades last year > 20. Query criteria must match every part of the business question, so the analyst combines both conditions with AND to return only Ohio clients who also traded more than 20 times. Using only one condition returns clients the brokerage did not ask for, and using OR returns everyone who meets either condition, producing a much larger, inaccurate list.
w: Using only the Ohio condition would return every Ohio client, including those who made few trades, which is more than the brokerage asked for.
Using only the trades condition would include active traders from every state, not just the Ohio clients the brokerage wants to reach.
Joining the conditions with OR returns anyone who lives in Ohio or traded often, creating a much larger list than the brokerage wants.

q.pt: Demonstrate advanced database applications
q.s: An auditor compares how often each leading digit appears in a company's expense amounts with the pattern predicted by Benford's Law. The auditor's main purpose is to
o: calculate the company's income tax liability.
detect possible fraud or manipulated data.
forecast the company's expenses for next year.
q.r: Detect possible fraud or manipulated data. Benford's Law describes how often each leading digit appears in many real data sets, with 1 leading about 30% of numbers. Invented or altered figures often depart from that pattern, so auditors use it to flag data for closer review. It does not calculate taxes, restructure database tables, or predict future expenses.
w: Income tax liability is figured from tax rules and taxable income, not by checking whether leading digits in expense amounts match an expected pattern.
Normalizing a database means reorganizing tables to remove repeated data, while the auditor is checking whether expense figures look made up or altered.
Comparing leading-digit patterns in past expenses helps spot suspicious numbers, but it does not predict how much the company will spend next year.

q.pt: Demonstrate advanced database applications
q.s: To produce one report that lists each customer's name next to that customer's loan balances, a database user links the Customers and Loans tables on their shared Customer ID field. This operation is a
q.r: Join. A join combines records from two or more tables by matching values in a shared field, such as a primary key in one table and the related foreign key in another. Joins let a query pull related data from several tables into one result. A filter limits which records appear, a sort changes their order, and a validation rule checks that entered data meets set conditions.
w: A filter limits which records appear, but the user is linking two tables through Customer ID to show names next to loan balances.
A sort changes the order of records, but it cannot combine the Customers and Loans tables into one report.
A validation rule checks that new data meets set conditions when entered, not how two tables are linked to produce a report.

q.pt: Demonstrate advanced database applications
q.s: In a bank's Accounts table, the field that uniquely identifies each record, such as the account number, is called the
q.r: Primary key. A primary key is a field whose value is unique for every record in a table, so each account can be identified and linked to related tables without confusion. A foreign key is a field in another table that refers to a primary key, a criteria field is used to set query conditions, and a calculated field computes a value from other fields.
w: A foreign key is a field in another table that points back to a primary key, so it is not the field that uniquely identifies each account in this table.
A criteria field is used to set conditions in a query, not to give every record in the Accounts table its own unique identifier.
A calculated field computes a value from other fields, such as a total, rather than uniquely identifying each account like an account number does.

q.pt: Demonstrate advanced database applications
q.s: A bank manager wants a query that shows the total value of deposits made at each branch last month. Which database feature should the query use?
o: A sort of customers by last name
A sum of deposit amounts grouped by branch
A filter showing only deposits under $100
A join to the employee schedule table
q.r: A sum of deposit amounts grouped by branch. An aggregate query groups records by a field, such as branch, and applies a calculation, such as sum, to produce one total per group, which answers the manager's question directly. Sorting customers by name does not total deposits, a filter for small deposits leaves out most of the data, and employee schedules are unrelated to deposit totals.
w: Sorting customers by last name only changes the order of the list; it does not add up deposits or separate them by branch.
Showing only deposits under $100 would leave out most deposits, so the totals for each branch would be far too low.
The employee schedule table has nothing to do with deposit amounts, so joining it would not help total each branch's deposits.

q.pt: Demonstrate advanced database applications
q.s: After running a query that joins the Customers and Loans tables, an analyst notices that several customers appear many more times than expected. What should the analyst do next?
o: Send the report because the query ran successfully
Delete the duplicate customers from the Customers table
Sort the results by customer name
Check the join fields and criteria for errors
q.r: Check the join fields and criteria for errors. Reviewing results for accuracy is the final step in building a query, and unexpected repeated records usually mean the tables were joined on the wrong field or the criteria are incomplete. Correcting the query design produces a reliable report. Sending flawed results spreads errors, deleting records from the database destroys real data, and sorting changes the order of the results without correcting them.
w: A query running without an error message does not mean the results are right; repeated customers are a clear sign something in the design is wrong.
The duplicates most likely come from a faulty join, not the Customers table, so deleting those records would destroy real data without fixing the query.
Sorting by name would only group the repeated rows together; it would not explain or fix why customers appear more times than expected.

q.pt: Comply with the spirit and intent of laws and regulations
q.s: A company discovers a loophole that lets it legally dump waste in a way that still harms a nearby river. The company is complying with the letter of the law but violating its
q.r: Spirit. The spirit of a law is its purpose or intent, such as protecting a river from pollution, while the letter of the law is its exact wording. Responsible businesses comply with both, because following only the wording while defeating the purpose is unethical and often leads to stricter regulation. Wording is another name for the letter of the law, jurisdiction is a court's authority, and precedent is an earlier court decision used as a guide.
w: Wording is the letter of the law, which the company is actually following; the question asks what it violates, which is the law's purpose.
Jurisdiction is a court's or government's authority over an area or case, not the purpose behind a law that the company is undermining.
Precedent is an earlier court decision used as a guide in later cases, not the intent of a law like protecting a river from pollution.

q.pt: Describe the nature of legally binding contracts
q.s: In a legally binding contract, the something of value that each party gives or promises to the other is called
q.r: Consideration. A legally binding contract requires an offer and acceptance, consideration, competent parties (capacity) and a legal purpose. Consideration is what each party exchanges, such as money, goods, services or a promise to act. Capacity is the legal ability to enter a contract, acceptance is agreeing to the terms of an offer, and legality means the contract's purpose must be lawful.
w: Capacity is a party's legal ability to enter a contract, such as being of age and sound mind, not the thing of value each side exchanges.
Acceptance is agreeing to the terms of an offer; it is a separate contract element from the money, goods or promises the parties trade.
Legality means the contract's purpose must be lawful, which is a requirement about the deal's purpose rather than the value each party gives.

q.pt: Describe methods used to protect intellectual property
q.s: A songwriter wants legal protection that prevents others from copying and selling an original song she wrote and recorded. Which form of intellectual property protection applies?
q.r: Copyright. A copyright protects original creative works, such as music, books, art, films and software, giving the creator exclusive rights to copy, sell and perform the work. A patent protects inventions and processes, a trademark protects words, names and symbols that identify a brand, and a trade secret is confidential business information, such as a formula, that is protected by keeping it private.
w: A patent protects inventions and new processes, not creative works like a song she wrote and recorded.
A trademark protects names, words and symbols that identify a brand, not the original music itself from being copied and sold.
A trade secret is protected by keeping information confidential, but a recorded song meant to be released can't stay secret and needs a different protection.

q.pt: Explain types of business ownership
q.s: Which form of business ownership is a separate legal entity whose owners' liability is generally limited to the amount they invested?
q.r: Corporation. A corporation is a business that is legally separate from its owners, the stockholders. It can own property, sue and be sued, and its owners usually risk only what they invested, which is called limited liability. Owners of a sole proprietorship and partners in a general partnership have unlimited liability for business debts, and a joint venture is a temporary arrangement between parties to complete a specific project.
w: A sole proprietorship is not separate from its owner, and that one owner has unlimited personal liability for all business debts.
In a general partnership the partners are personally responsible for business debts, so their liability is not limited to what they invested.
A joint venture is a temporary arrangement for a specific project, not a permanent separate legal entity defined by its owners' limited liability.

q.pt: Explain types of business ownership
q.s: Ava and Rob open a bike repair shop together. They share profits equally and are each personally responsible for all of the business's debts. Their business is a
q.r: General partnership. A general partnership is a business owned by two or more people who share in its management, profits and losses, and each partner has unlimited liability for business debts. In a limited partnership, at least one partner's liability is limited to his or her investment. A corporation's owners generally have limited liability, and a sole proprietorship has only one owner.
w: A limited partnership has at least one partner whose liability is limited, but here both Ava and Rob are personally responsible for all the debts.
A corporation is a separate legal entity whose owners usually have limited liability, which does not match two owners personally responsible for every debt.
A sole proprietorship has only one owner, but this shop is owned and run by two people who share the profits.

q.pt: Explain the nature of effective verbal communications
q.s: Instead of telling a new employee to "restock the shelf soon," Gina says, "Restock shelf 4 with the 12-ounce cans by 3 p.m." Gina is improving her verbal communication by
q.r: Using precise language. Precise speech means choosing specific words that convey your exact meaning so the listener does not have to guess. Gina names the shelf, the product and the deadline, which leaves little room for misunderstanding. Technical jargon consists of specialized terms that outsiders may not understand. Gina's revision is not more informal, and it does not depend on gestures or other nonverbal cues.
w: Technical jargon is specialized terms outsiders may not understand, but Gina used plain, specific details like a shelf number and a time.
Gina's revision isn't more casual; she simply replaced a vague request with exact details about what, where and when.
Gina's improvement is in her words, which now name the shelf, product and deadline, not in gestures or other nonverbal cues.

q.pt: Defend ideas objectively
q.s: Nadia proposes switching the store to an online scheduling app. When a coworker says the app costs too much, which response best defends her idea objectively?
o: Remind the coworker that she has worked there much longer
Say that the coworker always resists new ideas
Share data on the time and overtime the app would save
Insist on the app because she personally likes it
q.r: Share data on the time and overtime the app would save. Defending an idea objectively means supporting it with facts, logic and evidence rather than emotion or personal attacks. Showing projected time and overtime savings addresses the cost concern directly and lets others judge the idea on its merits. Pointing to seniority and criticizing the coworker are personal, not factual, arguments. Personal preference is subjective and does not explain why the idea benefits the business.
w: Pointing to how long she has worked there is about her status, not facts showing the app is worth its cost.
Saying the coworker always resists new ideas attacks the person instead of answering the concern about cost.
Liking the app personally is a subjective feeling that doesn't show how the app would benefit the store or justify its cost.

q.pt: Participate in group discussions
q.s: A project team agrees to every idea its popular leader proposes because members do not want to cause conflict or appear disloyal. This situation is an example of
q.r: Groupthink. Groupthink occurs when members conform to the group or its leader without critically evaluating ideas, often to avoid conflict. It can lead to poor decisions because alternatives and risks are never discussed. Consensus is genuine agreement that all members can support after open discussion. Brainstorming is generating many ideas without judging them, and active listening is concentrating fully on understanding a speaker.
w: Consensus is real agreement that members reach after open discussion, but this team goes along with the leader to avoid conflict without truly evaluating ideas.
Brainstorming means producing many ideas without judging them, while this team simply accepts whatever the leader proposes.
Active listening means focusing fully to understand a speaker, but the problem here is members agreeing without questioning the leader's ideas.

q.pt: Employ communication styles appropriate to target audience
q.s: Akira has five minutes to update senior executives on her team's project. Which communication style is most appropriate for this audience?
o: Detailed, walking through each daily task
Brief and direct, leading with key results
Casual, sharing the team's inside jokes
Technical, using the team's specialized terms
q.r: Brief and direct, leading with key results. Effective communicators adapt their style to the target audience. Senior executives are busy decision makers who want the bottom line first, followed by only the details they need to act. A step-by-step account of daily tasks wastes their limited time. A casual style with inside jokes is too informal for executives, and specialized team terms are jargon that may confuse listeners outside the project.
w: Walking through each daily task wastes the five minutes Akira has, since busy executives want the key results and only the details needed to act.
Inside jokes are too informal for senior executives and would not make sense to people outside Akira's team, wasting her short update.
The team's specialized terms are jargon that executives outside the project may not understand, which would make Akira's brief update harder to follow.

q.pt: Demonstrate active listening skills
q.s: While a frustrated customer explains how a late delivery disrupted her weekend event, Terrence tries to understand the situation from her point of view before he responds. Terrence is practicing
q.r: Empathetic listening. Empathetic listening means trying to understand a situation from the speaker's point of view and recognizing the feelings behind the words. It helps the listener respond with sensitivity and builds trust with customers. Selective listening is hearing only the parts of a message that interest the listener. Critical listening is evaluating a message to judge its accuracy or logic. Passive listening is receiving a message without engaging or responding.
w: Selective listening means hearing only the parts that interest you, while Terrence is trying to understand the whole situation from the customer's view.
Critical listening judges whether a message is accurate or logical, but Terrence is focused on seeing things from the customer's point of view.
Passive listening means taking in a message without engaging, yet Terrence is actively working to understand the customer's feelings before he responds.

q.pt: Explain communication techniques that support and encourage a speaker
q.s: Which of the following is an example of a verbal encourager that supports a speaker:
o: Checking the time on your phone
Changing the subject to your own story
q.r: Saying "Go on, I'm following you". Verbal encouragers are brief comments, such as "I see," "Really?" or "Go on," that show the listener is paying attention and invite the speaker to continue. They make the speaker feel heard and valued. Checking a phone signals boredom. Changing the subject shifts attention away from the speaker, and finishing the speaker's sentences is a form of interrupting that discourages the speaker from sharing.
w: Checking the time on your phone is a nonverbal sign of boredom, not a spoken comment that encourages the speaker to keep going.
Changing the subject to your own story pulls attention away from the speaker instead of inviting them to continue.
Finishing someone's sentences is a form of interrupting, which discourages the speaker rather than showing you're following along.

q.pt: Extract relevant information from written materials
q.s: Jamal needs to find the return deadline in a 10-page supplier agreement, so he quickly searches the document for the words "return" and "days." Jamal is
q.r: Scanning. Scanning is moving your eyes quickly over text to locate a specific piece of information, such as a name, number or key word. It lets a reader extract exactly what is needed without reading everything. Skimming is reading quickly to get the general idea of a document. Proofreading is checking writing for errors, and summarizing is restating the main points in a shorter form.
w: Skimming is reading quickly to get the general idea, but Jamal is hunting for one specific detail, the return deadline.
Proofreading checks writing for errors, but Jamal isn't correcting the agreement; he's searching it for a specific fact.
Summarizing means restating main points in shorter form, but Jamal is only trying to locate the return deadline.

q.pt: Write informational messages
q.s: A store manager emails employees that the break room will be repainted next Tuesday and will be closed from 8 a.m. until noon. This is a(n) __________ message.
q.r: Informational. An informational message shares routine facts, such as announcements, schedules or policy updates, that readers are expected to accept with a neutral or positive reaction. The manager is simply telling employees what will happen and when. A persuasive message tries to convince readers to act or agree. A bad-news message delivers disappointing information, and an inquiry requests information from the reader.
w: A persuasive message tries to convince readers to do or believe something, but the manager is only announcing when the break room will be closed.
A short break-room closure for painting is routine news readers should accept neutrally, not disappointing information that calls for a bad-news approach.
An inquiry asks the reader for information, but the manager's email gives employees facts instead of requesting anything from them.

q.pt: Write business letters
q.s: In a business letter, the phrase "Sincerely," that appears just before the writer's signature is called the
q.r: Complimentary close. The complimentary close is the polite ending phrase, such as "Sincerely," or "Respectfully," placed between the body of the letter and the signature. The salutation is the greeting, such as "Dear Mr. Chen:". The inside address contains the recipient's name, title, company and mailing address. Reference initials identify the person who typed or prepared the letter.
w: The salutation is the greeting at the start of the letter, such as "Dear Ms. Lopez:", not the closing phrase before the signature.
The inside address lists the recipient's name and mailing address near the top of the letter, not the polite phrase that comes before the signature.
Reference initials identify who typed or prepared the letter and appear below the signature block, not as the closing phrase like "Sincerely,".

q.pt: Handle phone calls in a businesslike manner
q.s: Before placing a business caller on hold, an employee should
o: transfer the call to a manager right away.
mute the line without saying anything to the caller.
ask the caller's permission and explain why.
tell the caller to call back later.
q.r: Ask the caller's permission and explain why. Telephone etiquette calls for asking whether the caller can hold, giving a brief reason and waiting for an answer. When returning, the employee should thank the caller for waiting. Transferring to a manager is unnecessary unless the manager is needed. Muting the line without explanation confuses the caller, and asking the caller to call back shifts the burden to the customer.
w: Transferring to a manager is unnecessary unless the manager is actually needed, and it skips asking the caller whether holding is okay.
Muting the line without a word leaves the caller confused about what is happening, which is poor telephone etiquette.
Telling the caller to call back pushes the burden onto the caller instead of politely asking to place the call on hold.

q.pt: Select and utilize appropriate formats for professional writing
q.s: In a full-block business letter, every part of the letter, including the date and the closing, begins at the
q.r: Left margin. In full-block (block) format, all letter parts are aligned at the left margin and paragraphs are not indented; a blank line separates paragraphs. This clean, efficient layout is the most widely used business letter style. No standard business letter format aligns its parts at the right margin or centers them. Modified-block format moves only the date and closing to the center point, and indenting to a tab stop is not used in full-block style.
w: Centering the date and closing is not part of full-block style; even modified-block style only moves those parts to the center point.
No standard business letter format lines its parts up at the right margin, and full-block style puts every part on the left.
Full-block style does not indent anything to a tab stop; every part, including the date and closing, starts at the same margin.

q.pt: Choose and use appropriate channel for workplace communication
q.s: A manager needs to tell an employee that his position is being eliminated. Which channel is most appropriate?
o: A notice on the break room bulletin board
A brief email sent after hours
q.r: A private face-to-face meeting. Sensitive or emotional messages require a rich channel that carries both verbal and nonverbal cues and allows immediate two-way discussion. A private face-to-face meeting shows respect, lets the manager answer questions and helps prevent misunderstanding. A group text and a bulletin board notice violate the employee's privacy. A brief email is a lean channel that seems impersonal for such serious news.
w: A group text exposes very private, upsetting news to other people and gives the employee no real chance to talk it through.
Posting a job elimination on the break room board makes private news public and gives the employee no way to ask questions.
An email is quick, but sending such serious news briefly and after hours feels cold and leaves the employee with no one to talk to.

q.pt: Select and use appropriate graphic aids
q.s: A coffee shop owner wants to show how drinks, pastries, sandwiches and merchandise each contributed to total monthly sales. Which graphic aid is most appropriate?
q.r: Pie chart. A pie chart is a circle divided into slices that show how each part contributes to a whole, so it clearly displays each category's share of total sales. A line graph is best for showing changes or trends over time. A flowchart shows the steps in a process, and an organizational chart shows the structure and reporting relationships within a business.
w: A line graph shows how values change over time, but the owner wants to show each category's share of one month's total sales.
A flowchart shows the steps in a process, not how drinks, pastries, sandwiches and merchandise each contributed to total sales.
An organizational chart shows a company's structure and who reports to whom, not how sales are divided among product categories.

q.pt: Write persuasive messages
q.s: In a persuasive sales letter, which element tells the reader exactly what to do next, such as calling to schedule a free consultation?
q.r: Call to action. A call to action is a specific request near the end of a persuasive message that tells the reader exactly what action to take and often how to take it easily. Without it, interested readers may not respond. A buffer is a neutral opening used to soften bad news. The inside address identifies the recipient, and an attention-getter opens the message to spark interest.
w: A buffer is a neutral opening used to soften bad news, not the part of a sales letter that tells the reader what to do next.
The inside address identifies the recipient at the top of the letter and does not ask the reader to take any action.
An attention-getter opens the message to spark interest, but the question asks for the element that tells the reader exactly what step to take next.

q.pt: Prepare simple written reports
q.s: A shift supervisor writes a one-page memo summarizing the number of customers served, problems encountered and tasks planned for the next day. This document is a(n)
q.r: Informal report. An informal report is a short, routine report, often written as a memo or email, that shares information within an organization. Daily activity reports like this one help managers track operations. A formal report is longer and researched, with sections such as a title page and table of contents. A business proposal recommends a plan to win approval, and an executive summary condenses a longer document.
w: A formal report is long and researched, with parts like a title page, while this is a short, routine one-page memo about the day's work.
A business proposal recommends a plan to win approval, but this memo just summarizes the day's activity and next day's tasks.
An executive summary condenses a longer document, but this memo stands on its own as a short daily report.

q.pt: Explain how digital communications (e.g., email, text messages, chats) exposes business to risk
q.s: An employee receives an email that appears to come from her company's IT department asking her to click a link and enter her password to "avoid account suspension." This message is most likely
q.r: A phishing attempt. Phishing is a fraudulent message designed to look legitimate so that recipients reveal passwords or other sensitive information. Urgent threats and requests for login details are common warning signs. If successful, phishing can lead to a data breach. A firewall blocks unauthorized network traffic, an acceptable use policy states rules for technology use, and encryption scrambles data to protect it.
w: A firewall alert would come from security software blocking network traffic, not an email asking the employee to click a link and type in her password.
An acceptable use policy is a set of company rules about using technology, not an urgent email demanding her password to avoid suspension.
A data encryption notice would explain how information is protected, but this email is trying to trick the employee into revealing her password.

q.pt: Follow oral directions
q.s: After her supervisor explains how to process an exchange, Leah says, "So I check the receipt, scan the returned item and then ring up the new one?" Why is Leah's response helpful?
o: It shows that she disagrees with the process
It confirms that she understood the directions correctly
It allows her to skip steps she already knows
It shifts responsibility for errors to the supervisor
q.r: It confirms that she understood the directions correctly. Restating oral directions gives the speaker feedback and a chance to correct any misunderstanding before the listener begins the task. This simple check reduces mistakes and rework. Leah's restatement does not signal disagreement, and it does not permit her to skip steps; it actually reinforces every step. Employees remain responsible for completing tasks correctly, so restating directions does not shift blame to the supervisor.
w: Leah repeats the steps back in order without objecting to any of them, so her response shows she is checking her understanding, not disagreeing.
Leah restates every step, including ones she might already know, so her response reinforces the full process rather than letting her skip parts of it.
Restating directions gives the supervisor a chance to correct her, but Leah is still responsible for doing the exchange correctly.

q.pt: Interpret others' nonverbal cues
q.s: Why should a salesperson avoid drawing a conclusion from a single nonverbal cue, such as a customer's crossed arms?
o: Nonverbal cues are usually meant to mislead others
Body language changes too quickly to observe
Nonverbal cues can be misinterpreted when viewed alone
Spoken words carry more meaning than body language
q.r: Nonverbal cues can be misinterpreted when viewed alone. A single nonverbal cue can have several meanings; crossed arms might signal defensiveness, or the customer might simply be cold. Skilled communicators look for cue clusters, several signals that point to the same meaning, and compare them with what the person says. Most nonverbal cues are not intended to mislead, body language can be observed throughout a conversation, and much of a message's meaning is carried by nonverbal behavior rather than by words alone.
w: Most nonverbal cues are not meant to mislead; the problem is that one cue like crossed arms can have several innocent meanings.
Body language can be watched throughout a conversation, so the issue isn't that it changes too fast but that one cue alone is unreliable.
Body language actually carries much of a message's meaning, so the reason for caution is that a single cue can be misread, not that it matters less.

q.pt: Apply written directions to achieve tasks
q.s: A new team member is assembling a display fixture using a printed instruction sheet. Which approach will most likely produce the correct result?
o: Look at the finished picture and assemble from memory
Complete the easiest steps first and return to the rest
Skim the sheet once and start building
Read each step and complete it before moving to the next
q.r: Read each step and complete it before moving to the next. Written directions are designed to be followed in sequence, so reading one step, completing it and then moving on reduces errors and missed details. Building from a picture or from memory skips information that the directions provide. Completing steps out of order can make later steps impossible or require rework. Skimming once does not give the reader enough attention to each step to complete the task accurately.
w: Building from the picture and memory skips details the written steps provide, making errors more likely on a fixture assembly.
Doing the easiest steps first breaks the intended order, which can make later steps impossible or force the new team member to redo work.
Skimming the sheet once gives only a general idea and misses details needed to assemble the fixture correctly.

q.pt: Provide legitimate responses to inquiries
q.s: A customer asks a drugstore clerk whether a cold medicine is safe to take with her prescription. The clerk is not sure. What is the most legitimate response?
o: Guess based on what other customers have said
Explain that he will ask the pharmacist to answer
Tell her the products are probably fine together
Suggest that she search for the answer online
q.r: Explain that he will ask the pharmacist to answer. A legitimate response to an inquiry is honest, accurate and complete. When an employee does not know the answer, he should say so and connect the customer with someone who does, especially when health or safety is involved. Guessing or offering a reassuring but unverified answer could harm the customer and the business. Sending the customer to search online fails to address her question.
w: Guessing based on other customers' comments could give her wrong information about a health and safety question.
Telling her the products are "probably fine" sounds reassuring but is an unverified guess that could put her health at risk.
Pointing her to an online search avoids the question instead of getting her an accurate answer from the pharmacist who can help.

q.pt: Identify sources that provide relevant, valid written material
q.s: When evaluating a website for a research report, Hannah checks whether the author is a recognized expert and whether the site cites its sources. Hannah is evaluating the website's
q.r: Credibility. Credibility is the trustworthiness and expertise of a source. An author's qualifications and a list of cited sources are strong signals that the information is valid and can be verified. Readability refers to how easy the text is to understand. Popularity, such as the number of visitors, does not prove accuracy, and an attractive design does not guarantee reliable content.
w: Readability is how easy the text is to understand, but Hannah is checking the author's expertise and sources to decide if the information is trustworthy.
Popularity measures how many people visit a site, which doesn't show whether the author is an expert or the information is supported.
Design is how the site looks, and an attractive layout says nothing about whether the author is qualified or the facts are cited.

q.pt: Give verbal directions
q.s: Before sending a new hire to the stockroom alone, Ms. Brandt explains the route and then asks him to describe it back to her. Ms. Brandt is
q.r: Checking for understanding. When giving verbal directions, the speaker should confirm that the listener can restate them correctly. Asking the listener to repeat or describe the directions reveals any confusion before the person sets out. Ms. Brandt is not demonstrating, which would involve showing the task, and her directions are spoken rather than written. Signal words show the order of steps but do not confirm understanding.
w: Demonstrating would mean showing the new hire the task, but Ms. Brandt explains the route and has him describe it back.
Ms. Brandt's directions are spoken, not written, and asking him to repeat them is a way to confirm he understood.
Signal words like "first" and "next" show the order of steps, but having him describe the route back is a check on his understanding.

q.pt: Ask relevant questions
q.s: A customer tells a sales associate she wants a laptop "for school." The associate replies, "What kinds of programs will you use for your classes?" The associate is asking a(n)
q.r: Probing question. A probing question is a follow-up that digs deeper into a previous answer to uncover more specific information. Here, the associate builds on the customer's general need to find the right product. A leading question is worded to suggest a particular answer. A closed question can be answered with yes, no or a brief fact, and a rhetorical question is asked for effect, without expecting an answer.
w: A leading question is worded to push the customer toward a certain answer, but the associate's open question lets her describe her own needs.
A closed question can be answered with yes, no or a short fact, while asking what programs she will use invites a detailed answer.
A rhetorical question is asked for effect without expecting an answer, but the associate truly wants to know which programs she will use.

q.pt: Utilize note-taking strategies
q.s: Sofia must take notes during a fast-paced vendor presentation. Which strategy will help her keep up while still recording accurate information?
o: Use abbreviations and symbols for common words
Write down every sentence the speaker says
Wait until the end and summarize from memory
Copy the slides word for word instead of listening
q.r: Use abbreviations and symbols for common words. Abbreviations and symbols, such as "w/" for with or an arrow for increase, let a note-taker record key ideas quickly without falling behind. Trying to write every sentence is impossible at a fast pace and causes the listener to miss ideas. Relying on memory leads to forgotten details.
